text.p: Italian bonds and futures had a droopy sort of a day after recent gains and dealers said they were taking the opportunity for a pause.

But several issues left a few furrowed brows, with Germany's shortfall in tax revenue unnerving the market because of its potential to upset the timing of European economic and monetary union (EMU). Finance Minister Theo Waigel said after the market closed the coalition would discuss additional budget measures and that Germany would meet the EMU deficit target.
June Btp LIFFE futures had an uneasy day testing lows at 129.99 and was 14 basis points off at 130.18 by 1537 GMT.

The February 2007 Btp ended 12 basis points down at 97.45 and was yielding 7.23 percent with the spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund at 153 basis points. Earlier today the spread had closed in to 148 basis points.

At home in Italy, players were sitting tight waiting for any indications of what the government's document of three-year rolling economic targets might contain in the way of broad outlines for state spending reforms. The so-called Dpef is due by the end of the month and will give an indication as to what structural measures the government intends to take in its efforts to meet and remain within EMU economic parameters.
However the leader of the upper house budget committee said the Dpef should be released next Thursday.

Preliminary inflation figures are also due next week and analysts are forecasting May inflation will slow to 1.5 percent year on year from 1.7 percent in April, which they hope may encourage the Bank of Italy into cutting the discount rate.

Abroad, eyes were on the U.S. although dealers said economic data released today gave mixed signals as to the strength of the economy and the likelihood of a fresh interest rate rise when the Fed's policy-making committee meets next week.
